status: TARGETED VERIFICATION PASS 2026-10-04. See verification.claims. Only the exact findings listed as confirmed are established by this pass. Other historical assertions remain provisional; counterfactual effects are design hypotheses, never facts or scheduled events.
how_to_use: Advance the hidden plots only through causes in the world: preconditions met, actors informed, time passed.
Reveal signals to the player through reports, envoys and rumours at plausible delays; never skip ahead.
If the player's actions change a precondition, change the plot; do not force the historical timeline back.
Keep the player capable of failing. Defeats, disgrace and lost provinces are legitimate outcomes.
Update hidden variables after each turn; keep them as ranges, not false precision.
Verification verdicts override earlier DOC/DOCUMENTED labels in legacy notes. A verified date, law or treaty does not verify motives, actual delivery or a counterfactual consequence.
Never apply a historical future event automatically after divergence. Hypotheses may drive fictional events only with explicit campaign-invention status and a recorded causal basis.
Do not use authorised troop quotas as mustered strength, whole-army totals as theatre strength, or historical casualties as universal rout thresholds.

systems.name: Money and credit
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Money exists in four states: promised, granted, collected, paid. Each step takes time and leaks. A promise is not coin.
rules: Model promised, authorised, collected, remitted and received funds separately. Delays depend on local records and campaign circumstances; there is no verified universal lag.

Confirmed legal baseline: Hungarian Act VIII protects noble fiscal privileges, while Act LXIII funds infantry and specifies other contributions, including town cash payments. Hungary is not exempt as a whole.
Credit and arrears can constrain operations; any precise interest, arrears duration or desertion response remains a design hypothesis until supported.
Occupation may disrupt current collections and seize cash as well as reduce future receipts. Silesia’s precise share of Habsburg revenue remains unverified.
British subsidy requires separate records of authorisation, remittance and receipt; do not assume automatic delay or automatic timely delivery.

systems.name: Bread, forage and the 1740 hunger
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Supply scarcity can constrain operations. Specific 1740–41 local harvest failures, grain prices and unrest levels remain unverified in this pass.
rules: Staff manage bread, forage, transport and quarters. Report consequential shortages and costs to the player.
Use local campaign evidence for stocks, routes, weather and requisitions. Do not manufacture historical price series or impose a universal few-days supply radius.

systems.name: The court and the council
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Power runs through the Geheime Konferenz, the ruler's trust, Francis Stephen's position and who controls access. Advice is partisan and often wrong.
rules: Khevenhüller is listed as Hofkriegsrat Vice-President in the 1740/41 personnel account (KA I pp. 309–310); appointment month and opening-date presence are unverified.
Exact Conference membership, access and motives require dated evidence. Rivalries and delays are possible campaign developments, not automatic properties of every minister.
A general’s command and ability to influence the ruler are distinct; track actual delegations and correspondence.

systems.name: The great powers
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Each power decides from its own interests and what it believes. They do not know what the player knows, and the player does not know what they will decide.
rules: PC I document 192 dates Gotter’s instructions to 8 December 1740; document 227 allows negotiation for part of Silesia. Do not force his demands to increase after every victory.
Treaties, perceived interests, resources and information constrain choices; the effectiveness of a player’s deterrence is contingent.
Sardinian cooperation with Austria began in 1742 according to the Swiss National Museum; the 1743 treaty was not its first involvement.
Courier delays and interception require a route and circumstances; exact durations remain assumptions.

systems.name: Estates, nobles and subjects
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Consent has to be bargained for, land by land. Each Estate has its own privileges, grievances and price.
rules: Different lands and social groups have different legal obligations; do not turn all Estates into one consent switch.
Hungarian Act LXIII authorises 21,622 infantry in six new regiments and separate mounted obligations. Actual mobilisation and arrival require returns.
A coronation or homage must be understood within its jurisdiction; a delay does not automatically erase every succession claim.
Local labour duties, poverty, recruiting and resistance require local evidence; avoid uniform national loyalty or unrest.

systems.name: Religion and legitimacy
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Religious affiliation, legal rights and institutional interests can matter without determining collective allegiance. Most proposed confessional reactions remain hypotheses.
rules: Treaty of Berlin (28 July 1742), article VI protects the Catholic religious status quo and Protestant freedom of conscience; enforcement remains a separate question.
Hungarian Act LXIII sections 13–16 sets obligations for clerical categories. Papal authorisation and total clerical remittances remain unverified.
The Prague expulsion decree dates to December 1744. Do not project it or allegations of collaboration back into 1741–42.
Papal neutrality, Hungarian Protestant concessions and Orthodox Frontier rights still need specific dated verification. Treat communities as internally diverse.

systems.name: The army and the field
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: The army on paper is not the army present. Silesia is nearly empty in December 1740; the Prussian army is much larger and ready.
rules: KA II pp. 58, 66 gives 7,359 in Silesia excluding Glatz, including garrisons, versus at least 26,000–27,000 Prussian invaders in late December 1740. KA I’s 99,446 is the whole Prussian army.
One Wallis regiment was present in October; 1,719 is its December return, not an October headcount.
KA II reconstructs Mollwitz strengths at 15,788 Austrian and 21,600 Prussian. These estimates do not define the tabletop demo’s counters.
The wooden/iron ramrod distinction does not establish sustained rates of fire or damage multipliers. The 1744 resolution is not a date of proven universal delivery.

Demo movement, fire, morale, casualty and visibility coefficients are uncalibrated design assumptions. Modern map terrain is a proxy. Results inform adjudication; they do not compel campaign outcomes.

systems.name: What reaches you, and when
systems.claim: mixed: explicit source-backed findings plus provisional simulation rules
systems.summary: Everything you know is old. Reports have senders, routes and reasons to lie.
rules: Each report carries a date, a sender and a route; couriers take days; absence of news is not safety.
Rumours may be true, half true or planted; label confidence honestly.
The player sees signals only through reports, envoys, letters and scouts.

KA1.type: 1896 official history citing archives; secondary, not contemporary testimony

KA2.location: vol. II, pp. 4–5, 58, opening of January 1741 chapter, 224–229, 245–246

H63.type: primary statute in published Hungarian translation

claims.claim: Gotter instructions dated 17 November 1740
claims.finding: Document 192 is dated Berlin, 8 December 1740; it refers to earlier instructions to Borcke. Do not conflate those instructions with Gotter’s commission.

claims.claim: Frederick’s price could only rise; partial cession was unavailable
claims.finding: On 26 December Frederick authorized Gotter to indicate willingness to accept a substantial part rather than all of Silesia. This documents an offer, not sincerity or certainty that agreement would last.

claims.claim: Sardinia joined openly only in 1743
claims.finding: The Swiss National Museum dates the Austrian–Sardinian Convention of Turin to 1 February 1742. Correct the 1743-only claim; the original convention was not opened, so this is secondary corroboration.

claims.claim: Khevenhüller listed as Hofkriegsrat Vice-President in 1740/41
claims.finding: The official history gives that office and cites the 1740 and 1741 court calendars. Appointment month and presence in Vienna on 21 October remain unverified.

claims.claim: Court factions, exact Conference roster, all guarantors’ legal obligations, envoys and courier times
claims.finding: The pass does not establish these from dated records. Preserve as research hypotheses; no categorical legal or personal-motive conclusions.

claims.claim: Mollwitz created the entire coalition from nothing
claims.finding: Document 344 refers to treaty negotiations already underway and a French letter dated 7 April. Victory may have affected commitment, but diplomacy did not begin only after 10 April.

claims.claim: Hungary paid only in men and loyalty, never cash
claims.finding: Act LXIII funds infantry from the country’s tax fund, and section 18 specifies cash contributions by towns in lieu of some mounted obligations. Noble exemption is not national fiscal exemption.

claims.claim: Silesian revenues secured foreign debt transferred by peace
claims.finding: Berlin article IX assigns debt owed to English and Dutch subjects to Prussia, subject to the Dutch settlement provision, while the queen retains debt owed to Brabant creditors. No principal amount verified.

claims.claim: Silesia supplied one tenth of revenue; treasury held 100,000 florins; grants took one to three quarters
claims.finding: No comparable dated fiscal series or cash account checked. Remove exact ratios, balances and fixed lags from the operating rules.

claims.claim: Regional grain-price curves and automatic 1740–41 famine unrest
claims.finding: The pass did not establish local harvest, price or mortality series. Weather background cannot determine a province’s unrest without local evidence.

claims.claim: Occupation affects only next year’s budget; British subsidy never arrives when needed
claims.finding: These absolutes are unsupported design rules. Occupation may interrupt current collections and seize chests; subsidy authorisation, remittance and receipt must be tracked separately. Exact British payment dates and sums remain unverified here.

claims.claim: The winter recovery was achieved by a cheap irregular army instead of the paid army
claims.finding: No cost comparison or force composition sufficient for that claim checked. Retain possible raids and operational successes without that causal verdict.

claims.claim: Hungarian noble tax privileges were reaffirmed
claims.finding: Act VIII protects the estates’ fiscal privileges. It does not show that all inhabitants or all forms of contribution were exempt.

claims.claim: 1741 infantry levy authorised
claims.finding: Act LXIII section 1 specifies 21,622 infantry in six new regiments; sections 1–2 specify funding and limits on replacement obligations. This is authorised establishment, not a verified muster or battlefield strength.

claims.claim: 60,000 Hungarian troops actually provided
claims.finding: Replace the unsourced delivered total with the 21,622 authorised infantry levy, separately from noble and mounted obligations. Actual mobilisation and arrival remain unverified.

claims.claim: Exact homage dates, a delayed coronation delays any claim, fixed robot burden, national loyalty blocs
claims.finding: No uniform constitutional or social rule is justified. Verify each jurisdiction, institution, date and locality; never treat a whole confession or province as one actor.

claims.claim: Catholic status quo protected in ceded Silesia
claims.finding: Berlin article VI protects the Catholic religious status quo alongside Protestant freedom of conscience and constrains sovereign interference. Treaty obligation is not proof of perfect enforcement.

claims.claim: Clerical obligations contributed to Hungarian mobilisation
claims.finding: Act LXIII sections 13–16 specify obligations for named clerical categories, with exemptions and assessment rules. It does not establish papal permission or a monarchy-wide cash total.

claims.claim: The Prague expulsion belongs to the 1741–42 opening
claims.finding: The decree is dated December 1744. It cannot be imported into 1741–42 as an event or proof of actual collaboration.

claims.claim: Papal neutrality, 1742 Protestant declaration, exact Carolina Resolutio effects, Orthodox Frontier privileges
claims.finding: No sufficient dated primary evidence opened for these specific claims. Leave provisional; do not hard-code confessional allegiance or a universal papal position.

claims.claim: 7,000 Austrians versus 100,000 Prussians invading Silesia
claims.finding: KA II counts 7,359 excluding Glatz against at least 26,000–27,000 invaders on Silesian soil in late December. KA I’s 99,446 is the whole Prussian army. The 7,359 includes garrisons and is not one field army.

claims.claim: 1,719 men in October 1740
claims.finding: KA II says one regiment was in Silesia in October, but explicitly takes 1,719 from December strength lists. Do not label it an October return.

claims.claim: Mollwitz force estimates in the official history
claims.finding: KA II p. 229 reconstructs 15,788 Austrians from post-battle returns plus losses; p. 224 gives 21,600 Prussians. Preserve source and estimation status. These totals do not map directly to the demo’s counters.

claims.claim: Austrian casualties imply a universal 29% rout threshold
claims.finding: KA II pp. 245–246 totals 4,551 Austrian personnel losses, including missing and prisoners as well as killed and wounded. Dividing by estimated strength describes one battle; it supplies no universal morale threshold.

claims.claim: Wooden ramrods prove a sustained 3:2 firing ratio
claims.finding: KA I pp. 381–382 describes wooden ramrods and a December 1744 resolution for iron ones. Equipment difference alone establishes neither battlefield sustained rates nor a damage multiplier; universal delivery by that date is not shown.

claims.claim: 1748 Principles document Frederick’s exact 1740 doctrine
claims.finding: The treatise was written in 1748 and circulated in 1753. Use as later reflection, not contemporary evidence that the novice king or every unit already behaved that way.

claims.claim: Demo speed, fire, morale, vision, strength and casualty coefficients
claims.finding: The 1.55 fire and 1.18 strength multipliers, movement speeds, 15-minute/12-phase cap and fog ranges remain game assumptions. No source supports substituting precise new coefficients in this pass.
